conflicts.issue: A breast case with no tissue (8000/3) or with cytology showing malignant cells of no type (8001/3) falls in XIIb by ICCC-2017. The tree refers it to Group XII.

ICCC-2017 places Myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3) and Mixed tumor, malignant, NOS (8940/3) in XIIa4 at every site, but the WHO breast table lists spindle cell or myoepithelial carcinoma as a subtype of metaplastic carcinoma, 8575/3, in XIf6. The report's words decide the group; registrar question 5.

Sarcomas of the breast go to Group IX. Malignant phyllodes tumour (9020/3), including periductal stromal tumour, stays in XIf6 by ICCC-2017, and a metaplastic carcinoma with chondroid or osseous differentiation (8575/3 or 8571/3) is a carcinoma, not a sarcoma. The sarcoma option carries a recognition aid against both misroutes.

Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma is a related term of 9715/3, which ICCC-2017 does not hold; the Group II tree carries 9715. Every breast lymphoma is referred to Group II and recorded at the breast.
Myeloid sarcoma in the breast is Ib; referred to Group I, keeping the breast site.

The WHO 2019 volume treats a choriocarcinomatous pattern as a pattern of invasive breast carcinoma of no special type. Applying Rule K to 'no special type with choriocarcinomatous pattern' would give Choriocarcinoma, NOS (9100/3), which ICCC-2017 places in Xb5 at the breast. Registrar question 2.

Within Group XI: a melanocytic pattern of no special type must not be coded to melanoma by Rule K (registrar question 2); melanoma goes to the melanoma tree (XId); Paget disease (8540/3) at the skin of the breast, C44.5, is XIe by ICCC-2017, while at the nipple, C50.0, it is XIf6.

data_gaps.need: A source reporting breast carcinoma in patients aged 0 to 18, naming its types (secretory carcinoma above all)
data_gaps.why: Pfister 2022 Table 3 (PDF p. 13) lists only juvenile fibroadenoma and juvenile papillomatosis at the breast, and neither breast source gives ages. Without a paediatric report every breast carcinoma, secretory carcinoma included, stays in the picker. With one, secretory carcinoma (8502/3) moves to br_histology as 'Secretory carcinoma (also called juvenile carcinoma)', reason 'Recorded as Secretory carcinoma (8502/3).' Settled 8 October 2026: Sosnowska-Sienkiewicz 2024 (PMC section 72) names secretory carcinoma the commonest invasive breast cancer in children and lists invasive ductal, invasive lobular, medullary, inflammatory and anaplastic carcinomas as less common; the six are now answers on br_histology, and registrar question 1 is answered by the 8 October ruling. The review gives no ages or case counts by type, so a population series remains wanted for frequency.
data_gaps.candidate_source: WHO Classification of Tumours, Breast Tumours, 5th edition (2019), secretory carcinoma chapter (age and ETV6::NTRK3); or WHO Classification of Paediatric Tumours, 5th edition (2022), breast chapter; or a population-based series of breast carcinoma under 20 years

registrar_questions: Secretory carcinoma. Pfister 2022 Table 3 (PDF p. 13) lists no breast carcinoma in children, and neither breast source gives ages, so every breast carcinoma, secretory carcinoma (8502/3) included, sits in the picker. ICD-O-3.2 lists Juvenile carcinoma of breast as a related term of 8502/3. Should secretory carcinoma wait in the picker until the controller fetches a paediatric source (data gap 1), or go on the breast histology screen now?

Special patterns of no special type. The WHO 2019 classification treats medullary, neuroendocrine-differentiated, pleomorphic, choriocarcinomatous, melanocytic, clear cell, oncocytic, lipid-rich, glycogen-rich and sebaceous carcinomas as patterns of invasive breast carcinoma of no special type (ICCR Invasive Breast 2022, PDF p. 12), and treats inflammatory carcinoma as a clinical presentation (Tan 2020, PDF p. 2). The ICCR table prints codes only beside oncocytic (8290/3), lipid-rich (8314/3), glycogen-rich (8315/3) and sebaceous (8410/3). Rule K would take the higher code for the others: Medullary carcinoma, NOS 8510/3, Carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation 8574/3, Inflammatory carcinoma 8530/3, Choriocarcinoma, NOS 9100/3 (Group X at the breast) and Malignant melanoma, NOS 8720/3 (XId). Proposed: a pattern with a printed code records that code; every other pattern records Infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS (8500/3); a report that names medullary carcinoma or inflammatory carcinoma as the diagnosis records 8510/3 or 8530/3. Which does the registrar rule?

Tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity. The WHO 2019 breast table (ICCR Invasive Breast 2022, PDF p. 14) gives it 8509/3, the code of invasive solid papillary carcinoma. ICD-O-3.2 prints no term for it at 8509/3. Confirm 8509/3, with the reason naming Solid papillary carcinoma with invasion.

Malignant adenomyoepithelioma. ICD-O-3.2 lists it as a synonym of Adenomyoepithelioma with carcinoma (8983/3); the ICCR table prints 8562/3 (Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma). The picker follows ICD-O-3.2. Confirm 8983/3.

Metaplastic carcinoma subtypes. The WHO table gives 8575/3 to every subtype. ICD-O-3.2 holds exact terms elsewhere: Fibromatosis-like metaplastic carcinoma 8572/3, Adenocarcinoma with chondroid differentiation 8571/3, Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS 8070/3, Spindle cell carcinoma, NOS 8032/3, Adenosquamous carcinoma 8560/3, and Myoepithelial carcinoma 8982/3, which ICCC-2017 places in Group XII. Proposed: a report that names metaplastic carcinoma with a subtype records 8575/3 (this also follows Rule K, as 8575 is the higher code); a report that names only the subtype records the ICD-O-3.2 term, and myoepithelial carcinoma named alone goes to Group XII. Which does the registrar rule?

Malignant phyllodes tumour. ICCC-2017 places 9020/3 at the breast in XIf6. It is offered on the fibroepithelial screen beside the benign and borderline grades and juvenile fibroadenoma, although no source here reports a malignant phyllodes tumour in a child (data gap 2). Keep it there, or move it to the picker?
